commonControls.name: Authentication and developer-token boundary
commonControls.description: Session authentication is backed by the identity store. Browser-cookie writes require same-origin and CSRF validation. Development tokens are disabled in production.

commonControls.name: Site selector reconciliation
commonControls.description: siteIdFor compares route, x-virgoscorpio-hub-site-id, query, and body selectors; rejects duplicated/conflicting/malformed selectors; resolves an explicit or membership-derived site; and verifies membership before route-specific capability checks.

commonControls.name: Capability authorization
commonControls.description: requireCapability delegates non-developer authorization to identity.authorizeSite. Some route families use path site IDs directly with this guard rather than siteIdFor; the route catalog calls out those differences for assessor verification.

commonControls.name: Own-content and collaboration authorization
commonControls.description: Content read/edit scope and collaboration-document authorization include ownership, document type, site and active-session checks where applicable.

The test confirms requester identifiers/profile details are not disclosed and Site A/Site B community snapshots, including the still-pending friendship, remain unchanged after denial. This is maintainer-authored regression coverage, not an exhaustive friendship/group lifecycle review or independent adversarial assessment.

families.title: Community conversations, messages, blocks, reports, moderation and notifications
families.authentication: Authenticated site member; moderation actions require stronger capability.
families.siteContext: Workflow helper extracts path site, invokes siteIdFor and binds conversation, recipient, message and report lookup to the same site.

coverage.limits: Existing A/B cases cover selected conversation/message/block/report/moderation/notification access and side effects. F1.49 adds live PostgreSQL coverage for POST /community/conversations: a Site B-only actor using a Site A-only recipient ID receives the existing non-disclosing 404 before the conversation transaction begins; deep before/after snapshots for both sites cover conversations, members, messages, notifications and the complete shared community-state projection; a same-site Site B create/reuse positive control returns the existing conversation without duplicate rows or notification fan-out. Complete workflow state transitions, other recipient variants, event fan-out outside the direct-create transaction, and independent adversarial/provider/realtime review remain separate. F1.50 adds a live PostgreSQL A/B regression for POST /api/v1/sites/{siteId}/community/friends/{userId}. Site B retains membership rows for invited and disabled users; the route must reject both, and foreign-site recipients, with the existing non-disclosing 404 before any friendship is written. Deep Site A/Site B snapshots prove denied attempts do not modify friendships or other community state. An active same-site recipient remains a positive control and produces one pending friendship. The friendship route implementation is in apps/api/src/platform-routes.js (friendRequest), while conversation workflows remain in packages/community/src/workflows.js. Broader friendship lifecycle, membership revocation races and independent adversarial/provider/realtime review remain separate.

families.title: Plugin registry, approvals, security review, activation and invocation
families.siteContext: Site resolved by siteIdFor; plugin lookup and all mutations bind both site ID and plugin ID.

coverage.limits: Live PostgreSQL A/B coverage verifies site-scoped plugin listing, non-disclosing foreign plugin IDs across approve/security-review/activate/disable/invoke, and no mutation or invocation records after denied cross-site actions. Conflicting registration site selectors are rejected before writes. The positive control approves a Site B plugin, requires a different Site B administrator for security review, and confirms activation/invocation remain fail-closed while execution is disabled. Actual isolated runner sandbox behavior and independent review remain external release gates.

families.title: Site firewall rules and shared policy cache
families.siteContext: Path site is resolved through siteIdFor; site-specific rules are capability-guarded. GET deliberately includes global rules where site_id is NULL.

coverage.limits: Denied capability is tested before tenant data access. Global/site precedence, cross-site rule visibility and cache invalidation require reviewer verification.

families.title: Cloud connection configuration and provider probes
families.siteContext: Site selected by siteIdFor; connection reads, tests, updates and disable operations must bind site ID and connection ID.

coverage.limits: Live PostgreSQL coverage verifies Site A/B listing isolation, non-disclosing 404s for foreign test/disable IDs, selector mismatch rejection with unchanged row state, and Site B positive controls using deliberately unresolved vault:// references so no provider calls occur. Real provider lifecycle, least-privilege provider IAM, egress/SSRF and live secret-manager behavior remain unverified.

families.title: Mega-menu configuration
families.siteContext: Path site is reconciled with optional header, query and JSON-body selectors through siteIdFor before route-specific authorization. GET requires content:read; create/update/delete require site:manage. Collection reads, versioned updates and deletes are scoped by site_id, with site/slug as the composite navigation key.
sideEffects: Metadata-only navigation.mega_menu_created, navigation.mega_menu_updated and navigation.mega_menu_deleted identity audit events

coverage.limits: Live PostgreSQL A/B route tests cover scoped listing, create, versioned update and delete with the same slug present in both sites. Foreign-site list/update/delete attempts and conflicting header/query/body selectors are rejected before mutation; snapshots prove both tenants remain unchanged after denial. The merged PR #92 regression races two updates with the same expected version and requires exactly one success, one version conflict, one version increment and a final row matching the winning request; the Site B same-slug row remains unchanged. F1.45 adds metadata-only identity audit events for create/update/delete on the same transaction queryable; unit tests prove callback ordering, fail-closed audit availability, stale-version behavior and rollback/retry for all three actions, while the live PostgreSQL route test injects audit_events trigger failures and proves database rollback plus exactly-one-event retry. Consumer rendering/cache invalidation, every presentation variant and independent adversarial review remain separate gates. F1.45 specifically validates the /mega-menus route family; the separate regular /menus route is tracked independently in the navigation-menus family.

families.title: Site navigation-menu configuration
families.siteContext: The path site is reconciled with optional header, query and JSON-body selectors before route authorization. GET requires content:read; create/update/delete require site:manage. Every read and mutation is scoped by site_id; update uses the existing expected-version condition.
sideEffects: Metadata-only navigation.menu_created, navigation.menu_updated and navigation.menu_deleted identity audit events commit on the same transaction queryable as the menu mutation.

coverage.limits: The route-capability suite verifies site:manage authorization before tenant data access. The F1.46 dedicated PostgreSQL integration injects audit_events trigger failures for create, update and delete, verifies the menu mutation and audit row roll back together, then verifies safe retry commits exactly one metadata-only correlated event; stale updates preserve 409 without audit and missing deletes preserve 404 without audit. The F1.47 two-site PostgreSQL regression uses identical slugs in Site A and Site B, an A-only actor, non-disclosing cross-site list/update/delete denials, menu and navigation-audit snapshots proving denied requests have no side effects, and positive Site A CRUD while preserving Site B state. Selector conflicts remain covered by tenant-isolation.integration.test.js. Cache/rendering behavior, broader role combinations and independent adversarial review remain separate gates.

families.title: Stripe billing webhook
families.siteContext: Tenant identity is bound through validated order/subscription metadata and database predicates, not a client-supplied site selector.

coverage.limits: Signed event and metadata-binding regressions use test doubles. Provider-generated payloads and two-site PostgreSQL callback execution remain external acceptance.

families.title: Presence HTTP, SSE, realtime events and WebSocket
families.authentication: Authenticated persistent session; WebSocket additionally enforces same-origin and reauthorizes commands.
families.siteContext: Presence HTTP, SSE and WebSocket upgrade routes reconcile the path site against x-virgoscorpio-hub-site-id and siteId query selectors before realtime capability authorization. Heartbeat JSON bodies also reconcile an optional siteId after bounded parsing and before presence operations. The generic membership precheck is disabled so the existing requireRealtimeCapability control remains the authorization gate. Per-command/document authorization, active-session and distributed Redis scope checks remain separate.

coverage.limits: Realtime tenant-isolation tests exercise conflicting header/query selectors for presence, SSE and WebSocket upgrades plus heartbeat body mismatch. Tests assert rejected upgrades create no subscriptions and rejected heartbeat mismatch leaves the existing presence lease unchanged. F1.26 merged in PR #131 at main 0748f56e01421d13121ec08f7bc036579e5406835. Exact PR-head #580/#581 and exact-main #582 all executed the real Redis 7.4 stop/restore scenario: both API bridges re-subscribed, a newly published site-scoped authorization invalidation reached the remote API node exactly once, only the revoked Site A socket closed before the test-only heartbeat, and Site B remained usable. Each hosted live DB/graph suite passed 92/92 with zero failures/skips; collaboration Playwright passed 4/4. The test proves a new event after reconnection, not replay/durable delivery of messages missed during outage. PostgreSQL remains authoritative and command/heartbeat reauthorization fallbacks remain required. PR #131 has no formal review submission; evidence is maintainer/automation only. Production Redis ACL/failover, independent deployment review and production distributed quota assessment remain open.

families.title: PostgreSQL outbox, delivery and worker execution
families.authentication: System worker; not an end-user HTTP route.
families.siteContext: Canonical event envelope carries schema version, site scope/classification, actor/resource identity and correlation; consumers validate subscription/scope before delivery.
capabilities: Worker identity and registered consumer subscription

coverage.limits: Envelope validation and retry/replay behavior have tests; hostile event injection, tenant teardown, all consumers and replay against a live multi-site dataset need independent review.

families.title: Memgraph projection and graph rebuild
families.siteContext: Projected graph nodes and relationships must carry site identity; query and rebuild paths must bind tenant plus aggregate/resource IDs and preserve version/tombstone ordering.

coverage.limits: Selected cross-site lookup and replay/rebuild behavior are tested. Forged envelopes, partition collisions, stale projection versions and site deletion cleanup require assessor review.

families.title: Redis presence and cross-instance realtime relay
families.authentication: Service-to-service adapter used by authenticated API streams.
families.siteContext: Channel/key naming and payload validation carry site scope; no user-provided raw channel or record data should be trusted.
capabilities: Redis service credentials and adapter configuration

coverage.limits: Unit and integration tests cover selected site-scoped channels, envelope validation, authorization invalidation and Redis outage fallback. F1.26 merged via PR #131 at main 0748f56e01421d13121ec08f7b320fd7621499f4. Exact PR-head workflows #580/#581 and exact-main workflow #582 executed the real Redis 7.4 stop/restore scenario: both API bridges re-subscribed, a new site-scoped authorization invalidation reached the remote API node exactly once, the revoked Site A socket closed, and Site B remained usable. Each hosted live PostgreSQL/Memgraph suite passed 92/92 with zero failures/skips; collaboration Playwright passed 4/4. The test proves delivery of a new event after reconnect, not replay or durable delivery of events lost during outage. PostgreSQL command/heartbeat reauthorization remains the fallback. Production Redis ACL, cluster/failover, network partition, durable invalidation and independent operational review remain open. PR #131 has no formal review submission; maintainer/automation evidence only.

families.title: Local library object reconciliation and storage adapters
families.authentication: Local operator/maintenance process; not a public HTTP route.
families.siteContext: Database references include local library assets, historical versions and media variants. The reconciler defaults to dry-run, rejects traversal and never follows symlinks.
capabilities: Local filesystem and PostgreSQL operator permissions
dataAccess: local filesystem or configured object-storage adapter
sideEffects: Dry-run reports orphan candidates; --apply deletes only eligible unreferenced local files.

coverage.limits: Local dry-run/traversal behavior is tested. Remote object storage, provider-side orphans, retention, concurrent reference creation and restore lifecycle are not covered by this reconciler test.
